text: Reuters reports that the central bank kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged after its scheduled policy meeting. Officials said inflation and employment data would continue to guide future decisions.
The transport ministry announced a new public bus schedule on Tuesday. The timetable will be published on the ministry website and stations before the changes take effect next month.
A university research team published its annual report after reviewing survey responses from students. The report lists the methodology, sample size, and findings in a public appendix.
The city council approved repairs for several roads following a public meeting. Officials said the work would be carried out in phases to reduce disruption to traffic.
The national weather service issued a routine advisory for heavy rainfall in several districts. Residents were asked to follow local emergency instructions and avoid flooded roads.
An election commission statement said polling staff would receive updated training before the next election. The notice included dates, locations, and contact information.
The health department opened registration for a vaccination drive at community clinics. Appointments are available during listed operating hours and require an identification document.
A technology company released its quarterly earnings statement. The filing includes revenue, operating expenses, and a comparison with the same quarter of the previous year.
Scientists published a paper describing a laboratory experiment on crop disease resistance. The authors reported the study design, controls, and limitations alongside the results.
The airport authority announced maintenance work on one terminal during the weekend. Some counters will move temporarily while signs direct passengers to alternate locations.
Social media users claim that eating a single common fruit instantly prevents every illness. The post provides no study, medical guidance, or source for the sweeping claim.
A viral post says a secret satellite signal will shut down every mobile phone at midnight worldwide. No technical evidence or official alert accompanies the claim.
An anonymous account claims that drinking a special mixture makes people immune to all infections within minutes. The message provides no clinical trial or medical source.
A message circulating online says the government has secretly cancelled every school examination. The post contains no official notice, date, order number, or education department statement.
A website claims a famous scientist discovered a machine that can predict exact lottery numbers forever. The article offers no reproducible experiment and asks readers to pay for access.
A viral headline says a city has moved its airport into the sea overnight. The story includes dramatic language but gives no official airport statement, engineering record, or location details.
An online post says a hidden law will automatically double every person's bank balance this week. It provides no legislation, regulator notice, or financial institution confirmation.
A chain message claims that placing a phone beside a glass of water charges the battery without electricity. No engineering explanation, test data, or manufacturer documentation is supplied.
A blog alleges that a single household spice can replace every medicine and cure all diseases. The article gives no evidence and discourages readers from seeking professional care.
A viral video caption says a new law requires everyone to register their pets at midnight today. The caption links only to an anonymous page rather than a government announcement.
